items.rationale: UPPER changes every letter to a capital and leaves the digit and hyphen alone, so Nbo-01 becomes NBO-01. LOWER would give nbo-01.
Excel's comparison operators ignore letter case, so the two texts are treated as equal and the result is TRUE. That is why case rarely breaks a lookup inside the sheet.
UPPER only changes the letters to capitals. ELDORET still has the same 7 characters as Eldoret, and LEN counts 7.

Inside Excel, case does not matter, but data often travels to other tools that are case-sensitive, and a standard form avoids surprises there. The other options are false: Excel compares lower-case text perfectly well, UPPER does not shorten text, and XLOOKUP ignores case.
